issuer.industry: Digital infrastructure engineering, deployment, and maintenance services

dimensions.name: Revenue growth and durability
dimensions.judgment: Growth and contract coverage are strong, but acquisitions, cancellable backlog, and discretionary customer budgets reduce durability.

dimensions.name: Profitability and cash flow
dimensions.judgment: Adjusted cash metrics are positive, but GAAP earnings weakened materially and operating cash flow lagged the company-defined measure.

dimensions.name: Market and competitive position
assumptions: No independent market-share dataset is included.
dimensions.judgment: Long-duration infrastructure demand and MSA coverage are attractive, but customers control work volumes and spending.

dimensions.name: Valuation quality
assumptions: The valuation uses 121,230,390 exchange-adjusted economic units and excludes the ungranted incentive-plan reserve from the base equity value.
No independent public-company peer set is included, so the score is deliberately penalized.
dimensions.judgment: The filing supports a reproducible IPO enterprise value of about $2.47bn, approximately 2.14x 2025 revenue and 16.63x company-defined Adjusted EBITDA. Those multiples require continued execution despite weak GAAP profitability, leverage, and limited peer benchmarking.

dimensions.name: Debt and balance-sheet resilience
dimensions.judgment: The IPO reduces leverage, but pro forma net debt remains about $526.5m, or roughly 3.55x 2025 Adjusted EBITDA.

dimensions.name: Use of proceeds
dimensions.judgment: Primary capital improves the balance sheet, but nearly all proceeds repay debt rather than fund a measurable growth program.

dimensions.name: Insider selling, lock-up, and dilution
assumptions: The base valuation excludes awards that have not yet been granted from the 12,123,039-share reserve.
dimensions.judgment: No base secondary sale is positive, but 101.7m continuing-owner shares or exchangeable units may become sale-eligible after 180 days, the initial incentive reserve equals about 10% of exchange-adjusted economic units, and the plan can grow annually by up to 5%.

dimensions.name: Governance and shareholder rights
dimensions.judgment: Continuing owners retain 83.90% of combined voting power, Oaktree can nominate six directors while holding at least 40%, and the Up-C/TRA structure materially limits minority influence.

dimensions.name: Legal and regulatory risk
assumptions: The assessment relies on issuer disclosure and is not an independent litigation or regulatory database search.
dimensions.judgment: The prospectus does not identify material ordinary-course litigation, but the labor-intensive operating model has meaningful OSHA, subcontractor, employment, government-funding, privacy, and project-compliance exposure.

dimensions.name: Disclosure quality and consistency
dimensions.judgment: Disclosure is detailed enough to reproduce the capital structure and key ratios, but the Up-C structure and non-GAAP measures require careful interpretation.

red_flags.title: Profitability weakened
red_flags.explanation: GAAP earnings fell sharply and Q1 2026 moved to a loss.

red_flags.title: IPO proceeds mainly repay debt
red_flags.explanation: The balance sheet improves, but pro forma net debt remains material.

red_flags.title: Continuing owners retain 83.90% control
red_flags.explanation: Public IPO buyers own only 16.10% of combined voting power and economic interests.

red_flags.title: Large post-lock-up and incentive overhang
red_flags.explanation: About 101.7m continuing-owner shares or exchangeable units may become sale-eligible after 180 days, and the initial incentive reserve is about 10% of exchange-adjusted economic units.

positive_signals.title: Revenue growth and MSA coverage
positive_signals.explanation: Revenue grew and most 2025 revenue was associated with multi-year MSAs.

positive_signals.title: Base offering is primary
positive_signals.explanation: The base shares were issued by the company rather than sold by existing holders.

positive_signals.title: Debt reduction is quantified
positive_signals.explanation: The filing clearly shows expected post-offering debt reduction.

positive_signals.title: No material ordinary-course litigation disclosed
positive_signals.explanation: The issuer states that ordinary-course matters are not expected to have a material adverse effect.

unknowns: No independent public-company peer set is included; valuation confidence is therefore medium rather than high.
The actual number, timing, and vesting of future awards from the incentive-plan reserve are not yet known.
Tax Receivable Agreement cash payments cannot be quantified from the final prospectus because they depend on future exchanges, tax attributes, and tax rates.
Independent human verification, conflict confirmation, and external legal-database review remain required before publication.

evidence.location: Consolidated Statements of Operations and MD&A
evidence.extracted_fact: Revenue rose from $997.996m in 2024 to $1,154.857m in 2025; $64.8m of 2025 revenue came from acquired businesses.
Multi-year MSAs represented about 92% of 2025 revenue; engineering and maintenance represented about 59%.

evidence.location: Financial statements, MD&A, and Non-GAAP Financial Measures
evidence.extracted_fact: Net income fell from $28.280m in 2024 to $6.214m in 2025; Q1 2026 recorded a $13.158m loss. Company-defined 2025 Free Cash Flow was $91.093m, operating cash flow was $12.3m, and Adjusted EBITDA was about $148.3m.
Pro forma cash was $1.870m and total indebtedness was $528.323m after the IPO. About $279.2m of net proceeds was allocated mainly to debt repayment.
ITG offered 19,512,196 Class A shares at $16.00; the base offering was primary, with an underwriter option for additional company shares.

evidence.location: Prospectus cover, Organizational Structure, Controlled Company, and Stockholders Agreement
evidence.extracted_fact: Continuing Equity Owners retained about 83.90% of combined voting power and economic interests after the base offering. The 62.45% figure applies only to the Class B/direct LLC-interest slice excluding Oaktree Blocked Fund's Class A position. Oaktree may nominate six directors while its group holds at least 40% of voting power.

TRA participants are expected to receive 85% of certain realized tax benefits; payments are expected to be substantial, unavailable for reinvestment, and may continue for more than fifteen years after all exchanges.

evidence.location: Risk Factors — customer spending and backlog
evidence.extracted_fact: Customers generally have no obligation to assign specific work volumes, their budgets may change quickly, and backlog may be cancelled or adjusted.

evidence.location: The Offering, Organizational Structure, Capitalization, and Summary Financial Data
evidence.extracted_fact: After the base offering there were 45,517,704 Class A shares and 75,712,686 exchangeable Class B/LLC units, or 121,230,390 exchange-adjusted economic units. At $16, implied equity value was about $1.940bn. Adding $528.323m pro forma debt and subtracting $1.870m cash gives about $2.466bn enterprise value, equal to about 2.14x 2025 revenue and 16.63x 2025 Adjusted EBITDA.

evidence.location: Shares Eligible for Future Sale and Underwriting
evidence.extracted_fact: The lock-up period is 180 days, subject to exceptions and possible early release by specified underwriters. The filing identifies 101,718,194 continuing-owner shares, including exchangeable LLC interests, as potentially sale-eligible beginning after the lock-up when permitted.

The initial incentive-plan reserve is 12,123,039 Class A shares, about 10.0% of exchange-adjusted economic units. The reserve may increase each January from 2027 through 2036 by up to 5% of outstanding Class A and Class B shares, subject to board determination.
ITG states that it is party to ordinary-course legal proceedings and claims that it believes will not have a material adverse effect on its business, financial condition, or results.

evidence.location: Risk Factors — workforce, subcontractors, safety, government funding, and regulatory compliance
evidence.extracted_fact: ITG operates hazardous project sites subject to OSHA; relies heavily on subcontractors; faces employment, workers' compensation, privacy, and project-compliance claims; and may incur delays or costs from government-funding and customer regulatory requirements.
